mainTopic: The limits on making חרם: how much one may dedicate, what counts as one's own, and whether כהנים and לוים may dedicate
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: the original owner gets first rights to buy back his field from הקדש only when his offer plus the added fifth brings הקדש more money than the other bidder's offer. A new משנה then teaches that a person may make חרם of part of each kind of property, but not all of it. רבי אליעזר says a חרם of everything does not take effect, and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה adds a קל וחומר: a person should certainly not give away all his property to people. The גמרא learns these rules from the wording of ויקרא 27:28. It explains why each category in the פסוק is needed and learns from the word ״בהמה״ that only what a person may always sell can be made חרם. It finds a practical difference between the two opinions in the תקנה of אושא: do not give more than a fifth to צדקה. A second משנה rules that one cannot make חרם of what is not truly his, and records a dispute about whether כהנים and לוים may make חרם. The גמרא concludes that everyone agrees לוים cannot make חרם of land, and they argue only about movables. The amud ends as רבי חייא בר אבין begins teaching that movable חרם may go to any כהן the owner chooses; his proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: When the owner gets first rights to redeem his field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pins down the case where the owners take precedence: the owner offered twenty-one, and with his added fifth his total payment beats the other bidder. Otherwise the field goes to the other bidder.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? Where the owner said twenty-one, the owners take precedence. And if not, the treasurer says to the other bidder: 'The field has come to you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an earlier discussion by explaining exactly when the original owner gets first rights to buy back his field from הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner must add a fifth (חומש) on top of what he offers. If he offers twenty-one, that extra fifth pushes his total payment above the other person's offer, so הקדש gains more by giving the field to the owner. If his total, even with the fifth, does not beat the other offer, the outsider gets the field.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? A request to define the exact situation
The owners come first and get first rights
It has reached you. The field is now yours

steps.whatToRemember: The owner gets priority only when his offer plus the added fifth brings הקדש more money than the other bidder's offer.

phrases.english: What is the case?
phrases.notes: This continues a discussion from the previous page about who gets to buy back a field from הקדש.

phrases.english: Where the owner said twenty-one,
the owners take precedence,
and if not,
he says to him: It has come to you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous page about redeeming fields from הקדש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what exact case do the owners take precedence?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the owner offered twenty-one, so that with his added fifth he pays more than the other bidder. Otherwise the field goes to the other bidder.

steps.title: A person may dedicate some, but not all, of his property
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a person may dedicate part of his flocks, cattle, Canaanite slaves, and ancestral field. If he dedicates all of them, the dedication does not take effect, according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may dedicate some of his sheep, some of his cattle, some of his Canaanite slaves and maidservants, and some of his ancestral field. But if he dedicated all of them, they are not dedicated. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches a limit on חרם: you may dedicate some of your property, but not all of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה goes through each type of property (animals, slaves, land) and allows dedicating part of each. רבי אליעזר goes further than a simple 'you shouldn't': if someone does dedicate everything, the חרם is not valid at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. The text the גמרא will discuss
Dedicates as חֵרֶם, a gift for holy or כֹּהֵן use
Canaanite slaves and maidservants, who count as the owner's property
An ancestral field inherited from one's family
They are not dedicated. The חֵרֶם does not take effect

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר is not only saying it is improper to dedicate everything. He says that a חרם of everything simply does not work.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A person may dedicate some of his flock and some of his cattle,
and some of his Canaanite slaves and maidservants,
and some of his ancestral field,
but if he dedicated all of them,
they are not dedicated,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may dedicate part of each kind of property. A dedication of all of it does not take effect (רבי אליעזר).

steps.title: A person should not give away all his property
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה argues with a קל וחומר: if a person may not dedicate everything even to Heaven, he certainly should be careful not to give all his property away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said: If even for Heaven a person may not dedicate all his property, how much more so should a person take care of his property.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the משנה, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה draws a lesson from the rule: protect your own property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He builds a קל וחומר. Giving to Heaven is the most worthy kind of giving, and even that has a limit. So giving everything away for less holy purposes, such as to other people, is certainly not proper.

keyTerms.meaning: The Most High. Giving to Heaven or to the holy
How much more so. The wording of a קַל וָחֹמֶר
An argument from a lighter case to a stronger case
Spares or takes care of his property

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the idea that a person should not give away everything he owns, even with good intentions.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said:
If for the Most High

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם רַשַּׁאי לְהַחְרִים כׇּל נְכָסָיו,
phrases.english: a person may not dedicate all his property,
how much more so
should a person spare his property!
phrases.notes: He means a person should not give all his property away to others either.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה אִם לַגָּבוֹהַּ אֵין אָדָם רַשַּׁאי לְהַחְרִים כׇּל נְכָסָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a broader lesson on top of רבי אליעזר's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Through a קל וחומר from הקדש, a person should guard his property and not give it all away.

steps.title: Where does this rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's rule that one may not dedicate everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the Torah source of the משנה's rule. It is setting up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated the limit without a source. The גמרא wants to see which פסוק teaches that only part of one's property may be dedicated.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion on the משנה
From where do we know these things? A request for a source

phrases.english: GEMARA:
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for limiting חרם to part of one's property.

steps.title: The פסוק says 'of' and not 'all'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the letter מ ('of', meaning 'some of') in each part of the פסוק: some of what he has, some people, some animals, some of the ancestral field, but never all.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: 'Of all that he has' means not all that he has. 'Of man' means not every man. 'Of animal' means not every animal. 'Of his ancestral field' means not all of his ancestral field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that finds the rule in the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each category in the פסוק begins with the letter מ, which means 'from' or 'some of'. The ברייתא reads each one as permission to dedicate only part of that category, which matches the list in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: From all that he has. Read as 'some of' what he owns
But not all

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: ״מִכׇּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ״ — וְלֹא כׇּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ,
phrases.english: "Of all that he has": but not all that he has,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:28. The little letter מ, meaning 'from', is what teaches 'some of'.

phrases.english: "Of man": but not every man,
"Of animal": but not every animal,
"Of ancestral field": but not all of the ancestral field.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִכׇּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ — וְלֹא כׇּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The letter מ in each phrase of ויקרא 27:28 limits the חרם to part of each category.

steps.title: The word 'אך' shows a חרם of everything does not take effect
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests the rule might only mean 'don't do it, but it works if you did'. It rejects this from the word אך, which shows that a חרם of everything is not valid, according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think he should not dedicate everything, but if he did, the property is dedicated. So the פסוק says 'אך' (only, notwithstanding). These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible weaker reading of the rule and then uses the word אך to prove the stronger reading in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'some of' alone might teach only that one should not dedicate everything from the start. The extra word אך, a word that limits, teaches that even after the fact such a חרם does not take effect. This is the source for 'אינם מוחרמים' in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: You might think. Introduces a possible mistaken idea
The Torah says. Brings the word of the פסוק that rejects that idea
Only or notwithstanding. A limiting word in the פסוק
They would be dedicated, meaning it works after the fact

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate lessons here: 'some of' teaches not to dedicate everything, and אך teaches that if you did, it does not work.

phrases.english: One might think he should not dedicate all,
but if he did dedicate, they would be dedicated?
The verse states: "Notwithstanding,"
phrases.notes: This is the first word of the same פסוק, ויקרא 27:28.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יַחְרִים, וְאִם הֶחְרִים יְהוּ מוּחְרָמִין? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: אַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and moves from 'should not' to 'does not take effect'.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's ruling in the משנה that a חרם of everything is not valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The limiting word אך in ויקרא 27:28.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's קל וחומר in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא repeats רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's קל וחומר: if a person may not give everything to Heaven, he should certainly take care of his property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said: If even for Heaven a person may not dedicate all his property, how much more so should a person take care of his property.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with the same statement of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה that appeared in the משנה, showing it is part of the same teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר learned his rule from the פסוק. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה takes that rule and draws a practical lesson for everyday life: do not give away everything you own.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted, allowed
To dedicate as חֵרֶם
All his property

steps.whatToRemember: One may dedicate only part of one's property. A חרם of everything is not valid (from אך), and a person should guard his property in general (קל וחומר).

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said:
If for the Most High

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם רַשַּׁאי לְהַחְרִים כׇּל נְכָסָיו,
phrases.english: a person may not dedicate all his property,
how much more so
should a person spare his property!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה: מָה אִם לַגָּבוֹהַּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא repeats the משנה's second opinion after giving the source for the first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should guard his property and not give it all away, learned by קל וחומר from הקדש.

steps.title: Why the verse needs every category
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that each word in the פסוק (all he has, man, ancestral field) is needed. Without each one, we would have made a wrong assumption about a different kind of property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Each word is needed. If the תורה had only said 'of all that he has,' I would think you just can't give away everything you own, but you could give away all of one kind of thing. So it says 'of man': not all your slaves. If it had only said 'of man,' I would think that is because a person can't manage without workers, but a field you could give away completely, since you can still make a living by sharecropping someone else's land. And if it had only said these two, I would think it is because both are a source of livelihood, but movable things you could give away entirely. So all of them are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא in Step 5 read 'some of' into each part of the פסוק. Now the גמרא explains why the תורה could not have written just one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a צריכותא: it shows that no single case teaches the others. 'All he has' alone would allow dedicating all of one kind. 'Man' alone could be explained by needing workers. 'Man' and 'field' together could be explained by livelihood. Each wrong idea is blocked by a different word.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary; the גמרא explains why each source or case had to be stated
The Merciful One; the תורה
I would have said; a wrong assumption the גמרא is ruling out
Sharecropping: working someone else's field for a share of the crop
Livelihood; a way to make a living
Movable property

steps.confusionAlert: The 'wrong ideas' here are not real opinions. They are only what we might have thought if the תורה had left out one of the words.

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
phrases.notes: He means: the פסוק had to mention every category separately.

phrases.english: for if the Merciful One had written only "of all that he has,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:28

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: כֹּל דְּאִית לֵיהּ לָא לַחְרֵים,
phrases.english: I would have said: everything he has, he may not dedicate,
but one type, let him dedicate all of it.
So the Merciful One wrote "of man": and not every man.
phrases.notes: 'Man' here means his slaves. Even within this one type, he can't dedicate all of them.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only "of man,"
[I would say that is] because he cannot manage without work being done,
but a field: he can manage by sharecropping.
And if it had taught us only these two,
[I would say it is] because here there is livelihood and here there is livelihood,
but movable property: let him dedicate all of it.
So they are all necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the derivation in Step 5 and justifies why every category in the פסוק is needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the פסוק need to list several categories instead of just one?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each category could have been explained by a reason that does not apply to the others (all of one type, needing workers, livelihood), so each must be written.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each category in ויקרא 27:28 (all he has, man, ancestral field) had to be written. Each could be explained by a reason that does not apply to the others: all of one type, needing workers, or livelihood.

steps.title: Why does the verse mention animals?
steps.stepSummary: The צריכותא did not use the word ״בהמה״, so the גמרא asks what that word teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the word 'animal'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא noticed that 'animal' was left out of the explanation above, so it asks what that word is for. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the other categories already teach the 'not everything' rule, ״בהמה״ looks extra. The גמרא expects that an extra word must teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? A question about a word that seems extra

phrases.english: "Animal": why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the צריכותא, which explained every category except ״בהמה״.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the word ״בהמה״ add to the פסוק?

steps.title: Only what you can sell can be dedicated
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא answers: ״בהמה״ teaches that, just like an animal, only something a person is allowed to sell can be made חרם. So a son, daughter, Hebrew slave or purchased field cannot be.
steps.simpleTranslation: As was taught: one might think a person can dedicate his son, his daughter, his Hebrew slave or maidservant, or a field he bought. So the verse says 'animal': just as an animal is something he may sell, so too he can dedicate only what he may sell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question from Step 9. The word 'animal' sets the model for what a person can dedicate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא compares everything to an animal, which its owner may freely sell. Things a person does not fully own the right to sell, like his children, a Hebrew slave, or a bought field, are left out. This is a new rule about what can be dedicated at all, not about 'not everything'.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think; introduces an idea the ברייתא will reject
The verse teaches; brings the פסוק that settles the question
A Jewish slave, who works for a set time and is not fully owned
A purchased field, as opposed to an inherited family field
Just as ... so too; a comparison that sets a rule

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic test for חרם: you can only dedicate what is truly yours to sell.

phrases.english: For that which was taught:
One might think a person may dedicate his son and his daughter,
his Hebrew slave and Hebrew maidservant,
and his purchased field?
The verse teaches: "animal,"

phrases.aramaic: מָה בְּהֵמָה יֵשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְמוֹכְרָהּ,
phrases.english: just as an animal is something he has permission to sell,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְמוֹכְרָהּ.
phrases.english: so too anything that he has permission to sell.
phrases.notes: The ending is left unsaid: only such things can be dedicated.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְכִדְתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל יַחְרִים אָדָם בְּנוֹ וּבִתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״בהמה״ teaches that only what a person may sell, like an animal, can be dedicated as חרם.

steps.title: But a father may sell his young daughter
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges its own rule: a father is allowed to sell his minor daughter as a maidservant, so by the rule he should be able to dedicate her.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a man is allowed to sell his young daughter. So should he be able to dedicate her?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tests its own rule from Step 10 with a case that seems to fit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule was 'whatever you may sell, you may dedicate.' A minor daughter can be sold as a maidservant, so the rule seems to allow dedicating her. Step 10 had listed the daughter as someone who cannot be dedicated, so the rule needs fixing.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so? Opens a challenge
His minor daughter, whom a father may sell as a maidservant

phrases.english: But his minor daughter:
he has permission to sell her,
phrases.notes: He may sell her as a Jewish maidservant.

phrases.english: so might he be able to dedicate her?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא בִּתּוֹ קְטַנָּה יֵשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְמוֹכְרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule set in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that whatever one may sell, one may dedicate.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A minor daughter may be sold, yet Step 10 counted her among those who cannot be dedicated.

steps.title: Only what you can sell forever
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא sharpens the rule: an animal can be sold forever, so only what a person can always sell can be dedicated. A daughter can be sold only while she is young, so she is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'animal': just as an animal can always be sold, so only what a person can always sell can be dedicated.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge by adding one word to the rule: 'forever' (always).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The right to sell an animal never runs out. A father's right to sell his daughter ends once she grows up, so it is not the same kind of right. With the added word 'forever', the daughter no longer fits the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Always, forever; with no time limit

steps.whatToRemember: ״בהמה״ teaches that only things a person may sell forever, like an animal, can be made חרם. Children, a Hebrew slave and a purchased field are left out.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "animal,"

phrases.aramaic: מָה בְּהֵמָה יֵשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְמוֹכְרָהּ לְעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: just as an animal is something he always has permission to sell,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְמוֹכְרָהּ לְעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: so too anything that he always has permission to sell.
phrases.notes: A daughter can only be sold while she is a minor, so she doesn't count.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״בְּהֵמָה״, מָה בְּהֵמָה יֵשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְמוֹכְרָהּ לְעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11 by refining the rule from Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refining the rule: adding the condition 'forever'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything a person may sell, even for a limited time, can be dedicated.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only what a person may always sell, like an animal, can be dedicated, so a minor daughter is excluded.

steps.title: Isn't רבי אלעזר בן עזריה saying the same thing as the תנא קמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר בן עזריה from the משנה and asks: his view sounds the same as the תנא קמא's, so what is he adding?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said: If a person may not give everything to Heaven, all the more so he should not give everything to people. But that is just what the תנא קמא said!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and challenges it: it seems to repeat the view of the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא (רבי אליעזר) already said a person may not make all his property הקדש. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says the same thing and adds a קל וחומר. If both reach the same result, why does the משנה record him as a separate voice?

keyTerms.meaning: To the Most High: giving to הקדש, to Heaven
This is the same as; used to point out that two views seem identical
The first תנא: the unnamed or first opinion in a משנה
Short for 'and so on'; the rest of the quote is assumed

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם לַגָּבוֹהַּ אֵין אָדָם רַשַּׁאי כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: If for the Most High a person is not permitted, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the line in the משנה: all the more so a person should spare his property and not give it all to people.

phrases.english: This is the same as the first Tanna!
phrases.notes: The first תנא here is רבי אליעזר, who said that if someone dedicates all his property, it does not take effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the end of the previous משנה to examine רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's statement in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His ruling seems to match the תנא קמא's, which would make it repetitive.

steps.title: The difference: the Usha rule about giving no more than a fifth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two views differ over רבי אילא's report of the תקנה of אושא: one who gives to צדקה should not give more than a fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a practical difference between them regarding רבי אילא's teaching. רבי אילא said: In אושא they made a rule that one who gives away his money should not give more than a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two opinions are not the same. They differ about how much a person may give away to צדקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's phrase 'all the more so for people' teaches a limit on giving even to ordinary causes. That fits the אושא rule of no more than a fifth. The תנא קמא did not say this, so by his view there is no such limit.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them: a practical case where the two views give different results
אושא, a town in the גליל where the חכמים made important תקנות
They enacted a rule (a תקנה)
One who spends freely; here, one who gives a lot to צדקה
A fifth

steps.whyThisMatters: The אושא rule of not giving more than a fifth of one's money to צדקה is a well-known guideline in הלכה.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them regarding the teaching of Rabbi Ila,
as Rabbi Ila said:
In Usha they enacted,
one who gives away freely should not give away more than a fifth.
phrases.notes: Giving away here means giving money to צדקה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by finding a practical difference between the two opinions.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical difference (נפקא מינה) between the two views
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two views seem identical, since both forbid dedicating everything.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה holds the אושא limit of a fifth for צדקה. The תנא קמא does not.
steps.whatToRemember: The two opinions differ over whether there is a one-fifth limit on giving to צדקה (the תקנה of אושא).

steps.title: A story about giving more than a fifth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells of someone who wanted to give more than a fifth and was stopped by a colleague. There are two versions of who was involved: רבי ישבב stopped someone, or רבי עקיבא stopped רבי ישבב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once someone wanted to give away more than a fifth, and his colleague did not let him. Who was the colleague? רבי ישבב. Some say רבי ישבב was the one who wanted to give, and his colleague did not let him. Who was that? רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story showing the one-fifth rule being followed in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that the חכמים actually enforced the limit, even on a generous person. The two versions differ only on who was giving and who was stopping. Either way, the person was stopped from giving more than a fifth.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story that really happened
And who was it?

phrases.english: There was an incident with someone who wanted
to give away more than a fifth,
and his colleague did not let him.
And who was it? Rabbi Yeshevav.
And some say: it was Rabbi Yeshevav who wanted to give,
and his colleague did not let him.
And who was it? Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לְבַזְבֵּז יוֹתֵר מֵחוֹמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the אושא rule from the previous step being applied in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים stopped a person from giving away more than a fifth.

steps.title: New משנה: You cannot dedicate what is not yours
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a person cannot make חרם his son, daughter, Hebrew slave or maidservant, or a field he bought, because these are not truly his.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone dedicates his son or daughter, his Hebrew slave or maidservant, or a field he bought, they are not dedicated, because a person cannot dedicate something that is not his.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists things a person cannot make חרם and gives the reason: they do not truly belong to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the same cases the ברייתא listed in steps 10–12. There the reason was that they cannot be sold forever; here the משנה says they are not fully his. A Hebrew slave goes free, and a bought field goes back to its original owner, so the owner does not hold them permanently.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks the start of a new משנה
One who makes something חרם, dedicating it
A Hebrew slave, a Jewish servant who goes free after a set time
A field he bought (not one he inherited); it returns to its original owner at the יובל
They are not dedicated; the חרם does not take effect

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the son or field becomes partly holy. The חרם simply does not take effect at all.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who dedicates his son or his daughter,
or his Hebrew slave or Hebrew maidservant,
or a field he bought —
phrases.notes: A bought field goes back to the original owner at the יובל, so the buyer does not own it forever.

phrases.english: they are not dedicated,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין אָדָם מַחְרִים דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ.
phrases.english: because a person cannot dedicate something that is not his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה. It matches the list of cases in the ברייתא from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חרם does not take effect on a son, daughter, Hebrew servants, or a purchased field, because they are not fully the person's own.

steps.title: Can כהנים and לוים dedicate their property?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says כהנים and לוים cannot make חרם. רבי שמעון says כהנים cannot, because חרמים go to them anyway, but לוים can, because חרמים do not go to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Priests and Levites cannot dedicate; this is רבי יהודה's view. רבי שמעון says: Priests cannot dedicate, because dedicated property belongs to them. Levites can dedicate, because dedicated property does not belong to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a dispute about whether כהנים and לוים can make their property חרם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון explains his view: a חרם goes to the כהנים, so a כהן making a חרם would just be giving it to himself. לוים do not receive חרמים, so their חרם works. The משנה does not give רבי יהודה's reason for including the לוים.

keyTerms.meaning: Priests
Levites
Dedicated property is theirs: חרמים are given to the כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees a כהן cannot make חרם. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון argue only about a לוי.

phrases.english: Priests and Levites do not dedicate,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Shimon says:
Priests do not dedicate,
because dedicated property is theirs,
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:14

phrases.english: but Levites do dedicate,
because dedicated property is not theirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a new case: who may make חרם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: כהנים and לוים cannot make חרם. רבי שמעון: כהנים cannot, because חרמים go to them; לוים can.

steps.title: רבי's compromise: land like רבי יהודה, movables like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי rules that לוים cannot make חרם of land, like רבי יהודה, but can make חרם of movable property, like רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: רבי יהודה seems right about land, because the פסוק says 'it is their eternal possession.' רבי שמעון seems right about movable things, because חרמים do not go to the לוים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with רבי giving a middle position between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון about whether לוים can make חרם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land of the לוים is called an אחוזת עולם, an eternal possession, so they cannot give it away as חרם. Movable things are different. חרמים go to the כהנים and not to the לוים, so when a לוי makes חרם he really gives something away, and that is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Land, real estate
Movable property, things you can carry
An eternal possession that can never truly leave the owner
Things dedicated as חרם, which are given to the כהנים

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּקַרְקָעוֹת,
phrases.english: Rabbi said: The words of Rabbi Yehuda seem right regarding land,
phrases.notes: Just "רבי" with no other name means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who put together the משנה.

phrases.english: as it says: "For it is an eternal possession for them,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:34

phrases.english: and the words of Rabbi Shimon seem right regarding movable property,
since the dedicated items are not theirs.
phrases.notes: He means חרמים go to the כהנים, not to the לוים.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: לוים cannot make חרם of land, but they can make חרם of movables.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּקַרְקָעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the משנה's argument from Step 17 with a compromise ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוים cannot make חרם of land, because it is an אחוזת עולם. They can make חרם of movables, because חרמים are not theirs.

steps.title: Why does רבי יהודה forbid לוים to dedicate movables?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to רבי יהודה, the land of the לוים is explained by the פסוק, but why can't they make חרם of movable things?
steps.simpleTranslation: As for רבי יהודה: it makes sense that כהנים cannot make חרם, since חרמים are theirs anyway. But the לוים? It makes sense they cannot make חרם of land, since it is written 'it is an eternal possession for them.' But let them make חרם of movables!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts its own discussion. It challenges רבי יהודה's view that לוים cannot make חרם at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא accepts that the כהנים rule has a reason, and that the land of the לוים has a reason too. But for the movable things of the לוים, neither reason seems to work, so why should רבי יהודה forbid them?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense that... (this part is fine, but here is the problem)
Let them dedicate (as חרם)

phrases.english: GEMARA: And according to Rabbi Yehuda,
it makes sense that priests cannot dedicate as חרם,
since dedicated items are theirs anyway,
but the Levites, why not?
It makes sense that they cannot dedicate land,
as it is written: "For it is an eternal possession for them,"
but let them dedicate movable property!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, בִּשְׁלָמָא כֹּהֲנִים אֵין מַחְרִימִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by asking for the source behind רבי יהודה's view in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that לוים cannot make חרם even of movables.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Neither reason given, that חרמים belong to them or that their land is an אחוזת עולם, applies to the movables of the לוים.

steps.title: A פסוק links movables to land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a פסוק puts movables and land side by side, so they follow the same rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'from all that he has... and from the field of his possession.' It compares movables to land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a פסוק that groups movables together with land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about חרם mentions 'all that he has,' meaning movables, right next to 'the field of his possession,' meaning land. This creates a הקש, a comparison that ties the two together. So for רבי יהודה, since לוים cannot make חרם of their land, they also cannot make חרם of their movables.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares, makes a הקש linking two things in one law
His ancestral (inherited) field

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר קְרָא: ״מִכֹּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ... וּמִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״
phrases.english: The verse says: "From all that he has... and from the field of his possession"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:28

phrases.english: it compares movable property to land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a source: a הקש from a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought movables have nothing to do with the land rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of the הקש, movables follow land, so לוים cannot make חרם of either.

steps.title: Why would רבי שמעון let לוים dedicate land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to רבי שמעון, movables make sense because he does not use the הקש, but how can לוים make חרם of land when the פסוק calls it an eternal possession?
steps.simpleTranslation: As for רבי שמעון: the כהנים rule is as we said. But the לוים? It makes sense they can make חרם of movables, since he does not use the הקש. But land, why? It is written 'it is an eternal possession for them'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי שמעון, who said לוים can make חרם, and challenges this for land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון does not accept the הקש, so it is easy to see why he allows movables. But the פסוק clearly says the land of the לוים is their אחוזת עולם, so it seems he could not allow them to make חרם of land.

keyTerms.meaning: As we already said
Why?
But it is written!

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Shimon,
it makes sense regarding priests, as we said,
but the Levites:
it makes sense that they may dedicate movables, since he does not make the comparison,
but land, why may they?
But it is written: "It is an eternal possession for them"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רבי יהודה, the גמרא now examines רבי שמעון the same way.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's general statement that לוים can make חרם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק 'אחוזת עולם' should stop לוים from making חרם of land, even without the הקש.

steps.title: רבי שמעון only meant movables
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that when רבי שמעון said לוים can make חרם, he only meant movable property.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does he mean by 'they can make חרם'? Movables.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing רבי שמעון's words: he was only talking about movables.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing changes in the law. The גמרא just reads רבי שמעון's statement in a limited way. He agrees that land cannot be made חרם by לוים, and he only allows movables.

keyTerms.meaning: What did he really mean when he said...?
They may dedicate as חרם

phrases.english: What is meant by "they may dedicate" that he said?
Movable property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the meaning of רבי שמעון's words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון allows לוים to make חרם of everything, including land.

steps.title: רבי's words suggest רבי שמעון did allow land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: רבי split land and movables between the two תנאים, which suggests רבי שמעון did allow land.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the end of the משנה says: רבי said, רבי יהודה seems right about land and רבי שמעון seems right about movables. Doesn't that show that רבי שמעון was also talking about land?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 22, using the wording of רבי's compromise in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי had to say that רבי יהודה is right about land, it sounds like רבי שמעון disagreed about land. That goes against the claim that רבי שמעון only meant movables.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of the משנה
By implication, from this we learn

phrases.english: But since the last part teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בִּמְקַרְקְעֵי
phrases.english: Rabbi said: The words of Rabbi Yehuda seem right regarding land
and the words of Rabbi Shimon regarding movables,

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְקַרְקְעֵי נָמֵי קָאָמַר?
phrases.english: doesn't that imply that Rabbi Shimon was talking about land too?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 22, using רבי's words from Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי שמעון only allowed movables.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי splitting the case between the two views suggests the two argued about land as well.

steps.title: Even רבי שמעון agrees about land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רבי: he means that רבי יהודה's view about land is accepted even by רבי שמעון, who only argued about movables.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: רבי said, רבי יהודה's words about land are accepted even by רבי שמעון, because רבי שמעון only argued about movables, and he agrees about land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 23 by explaining what רבי really meant. He was not taking sides on land. He was pointing out that both agree about land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's line is read as a description, not a ruling between two sides. On land, רבי שמעון agrees with רבי יהודה, so the only argument is about movables. This keeps the answer of Step 22 in place.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (rereading a statement)
Disagreed
Agrees, admits

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּקַרְקָעוֹת,
phrases.english: Rabbi said: The words of Rabbi Yehuda seem right to Rabbi Shimon regarding land,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לֹא נֶחְלַק אֶלָּא בְּמִטַּלְטְלִין,
phrases.english: since even Rabbi Shimon disagreed only about movables,
but regarding land he agrees with him.

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that לוים cannot make חרם of land. The argument is only about movables. רבי יהודה forbids them because of the הקש, and רבי שמעון allows them.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי as picking a winner on land. In this answer he is only saying that רבי שמעון already agrees with רבי יהודה there.
steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 23 and supports Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the wording of רבי's statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי was choosing רבי יהודה over רבי שמעון on land.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי says both agree about land. They argue only about movables.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: לוים can never make חרם of land. Movables are the only point of argument.

steps.title: Movable חרם may go to any כהן the owner chooses
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבין rules that movable property declared חרם may be given to whichever כהן the owner wants, and starts quoting a פסוק as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבין says: If someone declared his movable property חרם, he may give it to any כהן he wants, because the פסוק says: "Everything dedicated in Israel..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רבי חייא בר אבין: movable חרם can go to any כהן the owner picks. He begins quoting a פסוק to prove it, and the proof continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner of the חרם gets to choose which כהן receives it. The source is the פסוק that gives all חרם to the כהנים, which is quoted here only partly.

keyTerms.meaning: He declared something חרם, meaning he dedicated it so it goes to the כהנים
Movable property, as opposed to land
Any כהן he wants, so the owner chooses
Property dedicated through a חרם declaration

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a practical rule about how movable חרם is handed out: the owner chooses the כהן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin says:
One who dedicated movable property as חרם
may give it to any priest that he wishes,
as it is stated: "Everything dedicated in Israel
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:14. The פסוק keeps going in the next lines of the גמרא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of לוים and רבי שמעון and begins a new rule about who receives movable חרם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Movable property declared חרם may be given to any כהן the owner chooses, based on the פסוק "כל חרם בישראל".
